Medications That Can Cause Nutritional Deficiencies 
Nurses should know that chronic use of certain medications can cause nutritional deficiencies and negatively affect 
the musculoskeletal system. Not all individuals who take these drugs will develop nutritional deficiencies or 
musculoskeletal problems, but the risk increases with long-term use. Table 20.9 outlines some of the most common 
medications that can cause nutritional deficiencies related to the musculoskeletal system. 
Medication/Class 
Musculoskeletal Effect 
Considerations 
Corticosteroids 
Long-term use of corticosteroids, 
such as prednisone, can lead to 
decreased calcium absorption and 
increased calcium excretion, which 
can result in bone loss and 
osteoporosis. 
These medications can interfere 
with vitamin D metabolism, further 
affecting bone health.

inhibitors (PPIs) 
Long-term use of antacids or PPIs 
can impair the absorption of

B12, which are important for

PPI use may lead to
